ledger.x: 1291: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden unite.
1332: Lucerne joins the Confederacy ('1332 - Lucerne').
1351: Zurich joins ('1351 - Zurich').
1352: Glarus and Zug join ('1352 - Glarus, Zug').
1353: Bern joins ('1353 - Bern'), making the Eight Cantons.
1395: three border cells near Aarau, Biel and the Jura foot enter Cliopatria's shape.
1411: Appenzell becomes an associate ('associate since 1411'; it joins as the thirteenth member in 1513).
1415: the Confederacy conquers Aargau and sets up the County of Baden.

1416: the Upper Valais (Sieben Zenden) becomes a Zugewandter Ort (associate) of the Confederacy: 'Became a Zugewandter Ort in 1416 through an alliance with Uri, Unterwalden and Lucerne', 'followed by a treaty with Bern in 1446'.
1426: the Diet meets at Baden.
1440: Uri conquers the Leventina valley ('Uri conquered the Leventina Valley in 1440').

1454: St. Gallen allies with the Swiss. The abbey concluded a treaty in 1451 with Schwyz, Lucerne, Zurich and Glarus and the city one in 1454 with Schwyz, Lucerne, Zurich, Glarus, Zug and Bern: associates, drawn as Swiss by Cliopatria from 1459. Kept as a gain because the surrounding bailiwicks were Swiss and the…
1454: Schaffhausen becomes an associate ('associate from 1454'; a full member from 1501).
1460: the Confederacy conquers Thurgau.
1475: Bern attacks Vaud.
1475: the Valais extends its associate land.
1476: the fighting in Vaud ends with the victories at Grandson ('Charles was defeated in the Battle of Grandson') and Morat ('a devastating blow').
1476: the Confederacy keeps Grandson and Echallens in Vaud.
1481: Fribourg and Solothurn become members ('1481 - Fribourg, Solothurn'), making ten cantons after the Burgundian Wars.
1497: the Three Leagues of Graubunden ally with the Confederacy (the Grey League in 1497, the others in 1498: 'allied with the Old Swiss Confederacy').
1497: Blenio (Ticino) enters Cliopatria's shape.
1500: Uri, Schwyz and Nidwalden take Bellinzona.
1501: Basel and Schaffhausen join ('1501 - Basel, Schaffhausen'), making twelve cantons.
1512: the Swiss annex Locarno, the Maggia valley, Lugano and Mendrisio.
1512: the Ossola enters Cliopatria's shape.
1512: the Valtellina becomes a subject territory of the Three Leagues, the Confederacy's associate ('Valtellina: a subject territory from 1512 to 1797').
1513: after Novara the Swiss make Milan their protectorate.
1515: Marignano ends the Milan protectorate.
1516: the Swiss give the Ossola back to Milan; they keep Bellinzona and the other transmontane bailiwicks, now Ticino.
1526: Geneva allies with Bern and Fribourg.

1536: Bern and Fribourg conquer Vaud ('Vaud: Bern and Fribourg conquered it in 1536'); the Marignano page notes that Bern carried out this conquest on its own and that the Confederacy fought no war after 1525 apart from it.
1536: Bern occupies the Savoyard lands round Geneva.
1564: Savoy recovers the lands round Geneva; Bern keeps Vaud.
1620: the Valtellina leaves the Three Leagues.
1639: the Valtellina returns to the Three Leagues.
1713: the Diet leaves Baden (about 1712) for Frauenfeld.
1797: the Valtellina leaves the Three Leagues.
1798: the French overrun the Confederacy.
1798: the associate ends with the Confederacy.

1798: the Lower Valais, the associate's land since November 1475, ends with the Confederacy: the Lower Valais districts revolted against the Seven Tithings in 1798 and the Valais joined the Helvetic Republic.
1798: the Three Leagues end their association.
1798: France annexes Geneva.
1803: Napoleon's Act of Mediation restores the cantons.
1803: the cantons are restored.
1815: Neuchatel is a member canton.
1815: the Jura returns to Swiss land.
1815: Geneva joins the Confederacy.
1815: the Valais becomes a canton.
1815: the Federal Treaty.
20 November 1815: the Second Treaty of Paris.
ledger.cpn: Kingdom of France (Bourbon Restoration and July Monarchy)

ledger.x: 1816: Geneva's territory grows by treaty.
1848: Neuchatel becomes a republic.
1848: the federal state.
1848: Bern becomes the federal city.

wars.name: Battle of Sempach
wars.outcome: Swiss victory: 'At the Battle of Sempach in 1386, the Swiss defeated the Habsburgs.'

wars.name: Conquest of Aargau
wars.outcome: The Confederacy conquers Aargau and sets up the County of Baden.

wars.name: Old Zurich War
wars.outcome: 'Zurich was expelled from the Confederation from 1440 to 1450 due to a conflict over the territory of Toggenburg.'

wars.name: Conquest of Thurgau
wars.outcome: The Confederacy conquers Thurgau (the page: conquered in 1460) and exercises high justice there after 1499.

wars.name: Burgundian Wars
wars.outcome: Swiss (Lorrain-Swiss) victory over Charles the Bold: Grandson 1476, Morat 1476, Nancy 1477; the Confederacy kept Grandson, Morat and Echallens; Peace of Zurich on 24 January 1478 returned the Free County of Burgundy to Maximilian for 150,000 guilders.

wars.name: Swabian War
wars.outcome: Peace of Basel on 22 September 1499: the Confederacy exempted from imperial jurisdiction and taxes, 'a purely formal' imperial tie thereafter; 'The war caused no territorial changes except around Schaffhausen.'

wars.name: Battle of Marignano and the Swiss Italian campaigns
wars.outcome: Francis I wins at Marignano (13-14 September 1515); in the Perpetual Peace of Fribourg (29 November 1516) the Swiss renounce the Milan protectorate and return only the Ossola; Bellinzona and the other transmontane bailiwicks, now Ticino, remain Swiss.

wars.name: Bernese conquest of Vaud and the Genevan basin
wars.outcome: Bern and Fribourg conquer Vaud in 1536 and Bern occupies the Genevan basin; by the Treaty of Lausanne of 1564 Savoy recovers the lands round Geneva and Bern keeps Vaud 'forever'.

wars.name: Valtellina War
wars.outcome: The Three Leagues lost the Valtellina when rebels rose on 18/19 July 1620 (Graubünden page; History of Switzerland dates the loss to 1623, after the war from 1620); the Valtellina page gives a Valtellina War of 1620-1626 and a Treaty of Paris of February 1623.

wars.name: French invasion of Switzerland
wars.outcome: The Old Swiss Confederation collapsed; the Helvetic Republic, 'One and Indivisible', was proclaimed on 12 April 1798 without Geneva, Neuchatel and the Prince-Bishopric of Basel.

wars.name: Sonderbund War
wars.outcome: The Diet dissolved the Sonderbund on 21 October 1847; 'The Sonderbund was easily defeated in less than a month; there were about 130 killed.'

wars.name: Neuchatel crisis
wars.outcome: Royalists 'launched an armed insurrection on 3 September 1856'; under the Treaty of Paris of 26 May 1857 the King of Prussia 'finally renounced his claims to Neuchatel'.

certainty.note: Cantonal, bailiwick and associate frontiers were never surveyed; the Empire's legal frontier was loosened by the Peace of Basel (1499) and the Peace of Westphalia (1648) without a boundary line.
